sections.h2: Offices that touch an Indian River County tax bill
sections.html:
Responsibility is split three ways. The Property Appraiser sets values and accepts exemption filings, the Tax Collector mails and collects bills, and a county Value Adjustment Board hears appeals. Recorded deeds are kept by the Clerk of the Court.

The Property Appraiser has two offices, one in Vero at 1800 27th St., Bldg. B, Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469, and one in Sebastian at 1921 U.S. 1, (772) 226-1133, both open Monday through Friday from eight to five. The Tax Collector's tax department is at (772) 226-1343. As an agent for local governments, the Collector has no say over assessed value or the amount due.

Vero Beach, Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Orchid and Fellsmere are the municipalities in the county. A house in any of them is billed by the same county Tax Collector.

sections.h2: Due dates and early payment discounts
sections.html:
Bills go out by November 1. The early payment discount shrinks one step each month until March.

Discount by postmark month
Postmark monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchFull gross amount

A bill that never shows up in the mail is still the owner's responsibility. Anyone without one by about November 9 each year should call the Tax Collector. Send address changes in writing to the Property Appraiser, and expect a separate bill for every parcel you own.

Two messages on a bill deserve attention. "Do Not Pay" means a mortgage company has requested your original bill. "Back Taxes Remain Unpaid" means delinquent tax also sits on the account. Call (772) 226-1343 to learn the amount.

sections.h2: What if the bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
April 1 is the delinquency date, and a 3% penalty attaches to the gross tax. In May an advertising fee is added and the account is listed in a local newspaper once a week for three weeks. A certificate must then be sold by June 1.

The Tax Collector refers bidders to a county page on a tax certificate sale website. The certificate is a first lien on the parcel. Two years after the April 1 of issue, its holder may seek a deed, and the Clerk then auctions the property under the state's deposit and 24 hour payment rules.

Partial payments are not accepted on current or delinquent real estate bills. An owner who cannot pay in full has three routes: next year's installment plan, a homestead deferral if eligible, or a sale that clears the tax from proceeds.

sections.h2: Does Indian River County offer a four-payment plan?
sections.html:
Yes, provided next year's estimated bill is above $100. You apply before the plan year starts, and 2026 tax year applications are accepted November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027.

The plan has four bills: June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (no discount). June and September are computed from last year's tax, while December and March absorb the true-up to the new roll. A first payment made late, in July, loses the 6%. Skip it entirely and the account reverts to an ordinary November bill.

The office cannot accept an installment outside its month, and a payment that misses its month forfeits the discount. If the house sells mid-plan, the account stays on the plan for that year, so give the closing agent a list of the installments you paid. A buyer who would rather have an annual bill next year can ask the Tax Collector to drop the account.

A homestead owner whose age and income qualify may postpone part or all of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector by March 31. Interest builds on the deferred amount as a lien, and everything comes due at death, on a sale of the home, or when homestead status ends.

Homestead filings go to the Property Appraiser by March 1, and you must be a permanent Florida resident on January 1. A filing submitted after September 6 is applied to the 2027 tax year. The state exemption has two tiers, and the tier that also exempts school tax covers the first $25,000 only.

On a homestead, the Save Our Homes cap (2.7 percent for 2026) restrains growth. When the home sells, value resets to market the next January 1, so the buyer's bill may look nothing like yours.

sections.h2: How to petition against an Indian River County value
sections.html:
File with the Value Adjustment Board by the date printed on your Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. Florida sets that at 25 days after the notices are mailed. The Property Appraiser's home page links to the board's own site.

If the appraiser denies an exemption, you have 30 days from the mailing of the denial letter. Bring comparable sales, photographs and repair estimates with you. A petition built on a clear record of condition and recent sales is easier for a hearing officer to act on than a general complaint about the number.

sections.h2: If the bill arrives after the house has sold
sections.html:
A November notice follows the certified tax roll, which means it can land on someone who sold earlier in the year. The Tax Collector gives simple directions for that situation.

  • A real estate bill for property you no longer own should be forwarded to the new owner or returned to the Tax Collector's office.
  • A business equipment bill is different: if you owned the equipment on January 1, you still owe the tax. If you did not, call the Property Appraiser at (772) 226-1370.
  • Each parcel gets its own bill, so check that the legal description on yours matches everything you own.
  • Address changes go to the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector, and the appraiser offers an online change-of-address form.

Acting on a misdirected notice right away keeps it from turning into a delinquent account that a buyer's lender might spot.

Start by ordering a payoff and confirming which bill is open. The new owner is answerable for the whole November bill, but closing agents ordinarily prorate it and credit the buyer for the seller's months. Nothing goes to the Tax Collector as a partial payment from the seller. Keep a copy of every receipt and payoff letter for the closing file.

  • Look for a back-taxes message on the account.
  • List any installment payments already made.
  • Ask if a deferral lien is attached to the homestead.
  • Check the recorded deeds at the Clerk's office.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party on the document can be liable. Where back tax, a deferral lien or a damaged roof complicates a sale, a cash buyer taking the house as-is can have the title company pay the balance. Cash also skips lender appraisal and underwriting, which removes one common cause of delay.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Indian River County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the county tax payment portal that the Tax Collector links from its site. Discounts follow the postmark date, and the tax department at (772) 226-1343 can explain other payment options.

faqs.q: When does Indian River County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, when the 3% penalty is added. In May unpaid accounts are advertised, ahead of a certificate sale due by June 1.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the 2026 tax year installment plan?
faqs.a: Applications for the 2026 tax year run November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and the first payment falls in June.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of an Indian River County bill?
faqs.a: No. Partial payments on current or delinquent real estate bills are not accepted.

faqs.q: Do I owe the whole year's tax if I sell in spring?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the owner, but closing agents normally prorate, so the buyer repays the seller for the months after closing. Check the split on the closing statement.
